Theme Description: Emphasis on overall stance and body proportions, including limb configuration and general body mass or silhouette.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Identifications of bipedal vs. quadrupedal posture and basic limb presence.
Comparisons of forelimb length and robustness relative to body plan.

Theme Description: Cranial observations focusing on mouth shape, gape, teeth, eyes, nostrils, and jaw visibility/size.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Characterizations of mouth length, width, and how wide it opens.
Evaluations of tooth size and beak-like features related to feeding.
Notes on eyes, nostrils, head size, and jaw definition.

Theme Description: Axial features emphasizing neck length/profile and tail length/shape/curvature.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Length and curvature of the neck, including upward arches.
Tail length, thickness, curvature, and termination.

Theme Description: Descriptions of base coloration, patterning, and surface texture/markings.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Primary hues and general color notes, including uncertainty.
Stripes, outlines, spots, and ventral contrasts across body regions.
Notations of scales and spiky visual textures along the body and tail.

Theme Description: Structural features like spikes and cranial adornments, including speculations about their functions.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Rows of spikes or plates along the back and tail regions.
Crests, nose pieces, and fans with hypothesized roles in mating or thermoregulation.

Theme Description: Attention to foot form, claws/talons, hooks, and hoof-like structures.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Presence, size, and form of claws/nails, including weapon-like uses.
Observations of rear-foot hooks and hoof-like terminations, and their comparisons.

Theme Description: Inferences about diet, size, locomotion, function, and taxonomic similarity.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Plant- vs. meat-eating attributions and justifications for herbivory.
Size estimates and assumptions about speed and stability.
Hypotheses about the use of body parts for behavior, feeding, or defense.
Comparisons to known dinosaur groups or specific taxa to infer identity.

Theme Description: How the participant approaches description (what is prioritized) and expressions of uncertainty/confusion.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Prioritizing limbs, head, and structural outlines over coloration during observation.
Statements reflecting ambiguity, doubt, and difficulty with relationships or evolution.

Theme Description: Affective reactions and comparisons to toys, media, or modern animals to make sense of dinosaurs.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: References to toys, movies, and prior exposure informing recognition.
Evaluations of cuteness or scariness and related reactions.
Comparisons to living animals to describe appearance or function.
